title: Quantum advantage of nonlinear quantum battery and superconducting circuit implementation
authors: Wei-Jun Han, Peng-Yu Sun, Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract: A quantum battery is a novel energy storage device that operates on the principles of quantum mechanics. To enhance the charging performance of quantum batteries and further provide theoretical support for their physical implementation, we constructed an optical-field-dependent nonlinear quantum battery model. Meanwhile, we solved for the unbiased form of nonlinear interactions in this model, where the charging power of the proposed model exhibits a superlinear quantum advantage, and the charging time saturates the quantum speed limit. Through theoretical analysis, we confirm that this quantum advantage arises from the quantum effect of multiphoton absorption. Subsequently, with the derived nonlinear function form, we further investigated other properties of this nonlinear quantum battery. Finally, an experimental design scheme for this nonlinear quantum battery in superconducting quantum circuits is presented.
summary: The paper introduces an Optical-Field-Dependent Nonlinear Quantum Battery model that predicts a superlinear advantage in charging power due to multiphoton absorption. It provides both the rigorous theoretical derivation and a detailed experimental blueprint using superconducting circuits, successfully demonstrating that the achievable charging time saturates the fundamental quantum speed limit.
main_problem: To enhance the charging performance of quantum batteries (QBs) by developing a theoretical model for an optical-field-dependent nonlinear quantum battery and demonstrating its feasibility in superconducting circuits.
main_result: The proposed Nonlinear Quantum Battery exhibits a superlinear quantum advantage in charging power, confirming that this enhancement stems from multiphoton absorption effects. Furthermore, the experimental design successfully verifies that the charging time saturates the theoretical Quantum Speed Limit (QSL).
method: Theoretical analysis involves deriving an unbiased nonlinear interaction function by comparing energy metrics and QSL benchmarks; experimentally, it uses dispersive readout on superconducting circuits to measure charging time.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as an Optical-Field-Dependent Nonlinear Quantum Battery (O-NQB) comprising a two-level atom coupled to an optical cavity. The physical realization utilizes superconducting quantum circuits with tunable Josephson junctions, allowing precise control over the coupling strength and resonance conditions.

important_parameters: Nonlinearity order $k\geq2$, multiphoton absorption number $n$ (tunable in the range 2 to 6), detuning ($\Delta$), and coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on establishing an unbiased benchmark by equating QSL times across different models, eliminating arbitrary parameter tuning.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the O-NQB model, energy exchange dynamics in nonlinear QBs, and time evolution plots showing coherence decay and energy accumulation under varying detunings.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from theoretical modeling (deriving the Hamiltonian and finding the unbiased nonlinearity) to quantitative analysis (comparing charging metrics against the QSL benchmark), culminating in a detailed experimental design scheme using superconducting circuits for verification.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced quantum optics theory (nonlinear cavity QED, multiphoton effects) with cutting-edge solid-state hardware (superconducting qubits), providing concrete pathways to realizing enhanced energy storage devices based on fundamental quantum mechanics principles.
